title: Boolean word encoding
statement: For a Boolean mode, natural numbers $s,E,i$, a finite nondeterministic Turing machine $N$ over the Boolean alphabet, and Boolean words $x,\beta$, define a Boolean value as follows. If the mode is true, the value is true exactly when $i<2(2^E)^2+2\cdot 2^E+7$. Otherwise it is true when $i<2\cdot 2^E$, false when $i=2\cdot 2^E$, and true when $i=2\cdot 2^E+1$. For the remaining indices, it is the edge predicate for $N,x,s$ at the pair of indices $\left(\left\lfloor\frac{i-(2\cdot 2^E+2)}{2\cdot 2^E}\right\rfloor,\ (i-(2\cdot 2^E+2))\bmod 2^E\right)$ when $i-(2\cdot 2^E+2)<2(2^E)^2$; beyond that range it is the corresponding entry, if present, of the five-term Boolean list $(0,1,0,1,1)$, and false if there is no such entry.
hypotheses_covered: A finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
caveat: The payload does not define the edge predicate, and the parameters $s$ and $\beta$ do not occur in the displayed construction except that $s$ is passed to that predicate.
